one_liner: 32-bit x86 Linux userspace emulator for armhf with a dynarec; author's 2022 7-Zip test: about 4.5x QEMU, 2.6x FEX.
what_it_does: Box86 runs unmodified 32-bit x86 Linux programs (games, steamcmd, i386 Wine) on 32-bit ARM Linux as a user-mode emulator, launched as `box86 ./prog` or through binfmt_misc. It loads the x86 ELF itself but forwards calls into common system libraries (libc, libm, SDL, OpenGL, Vulkan, GTK and others) to native armhf builds through generated wrappers, emulating only libraries it has no wrapper for. It is a standalone tool, not an embeddable library; behaviour is tuned through BOX86_* environment variables and per-program box86rc profiles.
how_it_is_fast: The ARM dynarec translates x86 code in blocks over four passes (pass0 finds block extent and jumps, pass1 tracks flag use, pass2 sizes, pass3 emits), with a backward liveness pass (updateNeed) so x86 EFLAGS are only materialised when something reads them; MMX/SSE/SSE2 mostly map 1:1 onto NEON. Translated blocks are cached and guarded by page protection plus a hash signature, with a SIGSEGV handler catching writes to translated code. The biggest wins come from library wrapping, which runs GL, SDL or libc work at native speed, and from speed-over-accuracy defaults (STRONGMEM=0, FASTNAN=1, FASTROUND=1, x87 in float where possible).
when_to_use: Running closed-source 32-bit x86 Linux games and tools (GameMaker, Unity3D, older Steam titles, steamcmd) on ARM boards that can still run AArch32 userspace (Raspberry Pi 2-4, ODROID N2, RK3399/RK3588, Phytium D2000/FT2000).
Running i386 Wine on ARM next to Box64, which needs Box86 (or Box32) for the 32-bit components.
Programs that spend most of their time in wrapped libraries (OpenGL, SDL, Vulkan): the author's FOSDEM 2022 page shows glmark2 at 96-100% of native and OpenArena at 72-86%.
Replacing qemu-i386 user-mode when throughput matters more than exact x87 precision or x86 memory ordering.
when_not_to_use: 64-bit-only ARM CPUs or distributions without an armhf multiarch or chroot: Box86 needs a 32-bit userspace and a 32-bit toolchain and is 'useless on 64-bit only systems'; use Box64's experimental Box32 mode or FEX there.

Hand-optimised SIMD code, especially SSSE3: one SSSE3 op can expand to 10 NEON ops (pmaddubsw), and dav1d runs at only 21-55% of native on the FOSDEM page; CPU-bound integer code (7-Zip) sits at 40-61%.

Software that needs x86 memory ordering or exact x87, NaN and rounding behaviour: the fast defaults relax all three, and multithreaded JIT guests (Mono, JVM) are switched to BIGBLOCK=0 STRONGMEM=1, which is slower.
Non-ARM hosts or x86_64 binaries: the dynarec is ARM-only (other targets such as PowerPC LE run the interpreter), and 64-bit guests need Box64.
When you need fast upstream fixes: the repo is in low-cadence maintenance with 186 open issues, including dynarec-only failures such as #1042 (La-Mulana runs only with dynarec disabled).

integration.form: standalone executable (CMake build from source, installs the box86 binary, a binfmt_misc entry, bundled x86 libs and /etc/box86.box86rc; Debian packaging in debian/)
integration.dependencies: armhf (32-bit) libc plus the 32-bit native libraries to be wrapped (SDL, OpenGL or gl4es, Vulkan); optional Zydis for TRACE builds; ccache recommended for development
integration.min_toolchain: CMake 3.10+, a 32-bit ARM GCC (gcc-arm-linux-gnueabihf on aarch64 hosts), -std=gnu11; docs recommend -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo with a board profile (-DRPI4=1, -DODROIDN2=1, -DRK3588=1 ...)
integration.platforms: 32-bit little-endian ARM Linux userspace (armhf) on ARMv7, or on ARMv8 CPUs that keep AArch32 at EL0 with a multiarch or chroot setup; dynarec for ARM only
integration.thread_safety: Emulates multithreaded guests; dynarec block building (FillBlock) is not multithreaded, and BOX86_DYNAREC_WAIT chooses whether other threads wait for it or fall back to the interpreter
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: replaces qemu-i386 user-mode via binfmt_misc for x86 Linux binaries, but only on armhf userspaces, with relaxed x87 and memory-ordering defaults, and some programs need per-app box86rc profiles

gotchas: Config precedence is inverted from what most tools do: ~/.box86rc beats /etc/box86.box86rc, which beats the command line, so BOX86_* variables you set when benchmarking can be silently overridden by a shipped per-program profile.
JIT'd guest code is tracked with memory protection and a SIGSEGV handler, so gdb stops on many 'normal' segfaults; use `handle SIGSEGV nostop` and break in my_box86signalhandler.

Several correctness fixes landed in September 2026 after the newest CHANGELOG entry (v0.3.8): a use-after-free in aligned_realloc, a CVTTPS2PI lower-lane bounds check, an atfork loop out-of-bounds, interpreter LOCK 16-bit INC/DEC; build from master rather than an old package.

The QEMU and FEX numbers come from a 2022 article by the Box86 author, read here only through search-result text: the machine, the QEMU, FEX and Box86 versions and the build flags are not visible; QEMU and FEX keep 80-bit x87 in softfloat while Box uses hardware float, and 7-Zip's built-in benchmark ('7z b') runs one thread per core by default (4 threads in the FOSDEM sample output), so the scores also reflect each emulator's threading and atomics handling.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Box86 over FEX or QEMU user-mode when the guest is 32-bit x86 and the host can run armhf: in the author's 2022 7-Zip run it reached about 50% of native against 19% for FEX and 11% for QEMU. Use Box64 for x86_64 guests (or its Box32 mode on 64-bit-only hosts), FEX on aarch64-only hardware or when you want stricter x86 semantics, and Blink to run x86-64 Linux programs on non-ARM hosts.
verified_claims_summary: In the Box86 author's March 2022 box86.org comparison (EGRESS_BLOCKED here; numbers from search-result text, which also says the 7-Zip build was version 16 from Ubuntu), 7-Zip as a 32-bit x86 guest scored Box86 3117 MIPS against native ARM 6157, FEX 1197 and QEMU user-mode 691, about 4.5x QEMU and 2.6x FEX (derived from snippet data), with no CPU, emulator versions or flags visible. The author's FOSDEM 2022 page gives hardware-labelled Box86-versus-native numbers only (7-Zip 16.02 'Tot' 40-61% of native across seven boards, e.g. ODROID N2 3811 vs 8981; dav1d 21-55%; glmark2 96-100%; OpenArena 72-86%), and the README's '5 to 10 times faster' DynaRec figure is against its own interpreter with no workload stated.
status_note: MIT-licensed, 3.8k stars and not archived, but in low-cadence maintenance (about 15 commits between 2025-06-22 and 2026-09-27, mostly opcodes, wrappers and bug fixes) while the Box64 README now offers Box32 as an alternative for 32-bit binaries; still the standard way to run i386 Linux binaries on armhf.
